History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with a PMH significant for 
chronic pancreatitis secondary to CFTR mutation, depression and 
anxiety, upper extremity DVT, and anemia that presents with 
epigastric pain that radiates to her back and is accompanied by 
nausea and vomiting.  Her pain occurs in two characters.  It is 
a throbbing dull pain that sits in her epigastrum, and at times 
increases in intensity and becomes sharp with radiation to her 
back.  She has been have this pain since ___.
.
Last week she had a cold and cough with rhinorrhea, mild sore 
throat for which she was treated with azithromycin. She has had 
upper respiratory tract infections that have precipitated the 
epigastric pain triggered episodes in the past per the patients 
report.  She has had over thirty admissions for abdominal pain 
in the past and has had a regimen developed to treat the nausea, 
pain, and anxiety.  Over the course of the past week she has 
developed epigastric pain that is the same pain as her prior 
episodes of pancreatitis.  She has had associated nausea and 
vomiting, with as many as 10 episodes of emesis a day. Since 
___ she has been dry heaving without any vomiting.  Also, she 
reports that she has not urinated since last night. She denies 
any fever or chills or diarrhea.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with a PMH of CFTR minor 
mutation complicated by chronic pancreatitis with multiple 
admissions.  She presents with epigastric pain, nausea and 
vomiting that is consistent with her prior episodes of 
pancreatitis. 
.
# Bacteremia: Venous access is a constant issue in Ms. ___, 
and on the first day of admission she began to lose peripheral 
access.  She was requiring IV access for nausea and pain 
control. A PICC was placed and 1.5 days later she spiked a fever 
to 103.7. She grew out Klebsiella bacteremia on ___ and 
___.  Originally she was started on Vancomycin and Zosyn, 
and switched to Vancomycin and Cefepime. Sensitivities came back 
sensitive to cipro.  She was transitioned to PO, and missed a 
dose because she fell asleep, the following day she spiked to 
102.9. She was started back on IV antibiotics with ceftriaxone 
and she defervesced.  All cultures after the second were 
negative.
.
#  Pancreatitis: Patient with frequent admissions for chronic 
pancreatitis.  She has been followed by Dr. ___ this 
issue in the past and has an established regimen that she 
recieves when she is admitted for pancreatitis: IV dilaudid 8mg 
q2 PRN, ketorolac 15mg IV q6 PRN x 3 days, ativan 0.5-1mg q4 
PRN, promethazine 25 mg IV Q4H PRN and zofran 4mg IV q8 PRN. She 
was switched to compazine, because she had peripheral access and 
phenergan is a vesicant.  She improved slowly over the course of 
the admission and was stable on discharge.
.
# Anemia/Thrombocytopenia: She had transient anemia and 
thrombocytopenia in the setting of her infection.  Likely as a 
result of her bacteremia or her medication regimen.  Her 
platelets and HCT rebounded with treatment of her infection and 
when the change was made to Cipro/ceftriaxone. 
.
.
#  DVT in LUE: Developed after PICC placement during prior 
admission in ___.  She was undergoing anticoagulation 
for 3 months with lovenox but she became thrombocytopenic HIT 
was considered with low suspicion, but she was switched to 
fondiparinux and then transitioned back to lovenox. She is on 
coumadin as an outpatient. We held coumadin in house because of 
questionable absorption.
.  
#  Anxiety/Depression: She is on a home regimen of Ativan 1mg PO 
q4H as needed for anxiety.  We continued her home regimen.

Discharge Instructions:
Ms. ___, it was a pleasure taking part in your care.  You were 
admitted to ___ for chronic pancreatitis flare causing severe 
abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting.  You were started on IV 
pain and nausea control and given IV fluids.  We did not let you 
eat for the first few days because we wanted to rest your bowels 
to reduce the inflammation from your pancreatitis. 
.
We placed IVs in your hand and arm, but during the same day they 
were malfunctioning.  You have a history of being a very 
difficult person to place IVs on and you requested a PICC, and 
after discussion with the team we decided to place a PICC for IV 
medication administration.  1.5 days after placement of your 
PICC placement you developed a fever and we found there to be an 
infection in your blood.  You were treated with IV antibiotics 
while you were not taking anything by mouth and were then 
switched to pills. We pulled the PICC line and placed an IV in 
your other arm.  At the time of discharge you were improved from 
admission.
.
During your stay, we made the following CHANGES to your 
medications:
We ADDED Ceftriaxone 2gm IV once a day.  Please take this 
antibiotic until ___.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with chronic pancreatitis and poor IV access
and need for hydration and meds.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ was the attending who supervised throughout.
Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the patent right
brachial vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and
immediately after establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was
then placed over a guidewire and a 4 ___ single-lumen PICC line measuring
41 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip
positioned in the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter
was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.  The peel-away sheath
and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was secured to the skin,
flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided 4 ___
single-lumen PICC line placement via the right brachial venous approach. Final
internal length is 41 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready
to use.

INDICATION:  ___ female with chronic pancreatitis, presents with fever
to 103.7 and Gram-negative rod bacteremia.  Evaluate for abscess, fluid
collection, or any other acute intra-abdominal process.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis without IV contrast.  Oral contrast was administered.  Coronal and
sagittal reformats were displayed.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  There is minimal subsegmental dependent
atelectasis, but the lung bases are otherwise clear.  The liver, spleen, and
bilateral adrenal glands are normal.  The gallbladder is surgically absent. 
There is no peripancreatic stranding or fluid collection.  The opacified
stomach and intra-abdominal loops of small bowel are unremarkable.  A
jejunostomy tube is noted in situ.  There is no free air or fluid in the
abdomen.  Small mesenteric nodes do not meet CT criteria for pathologic
enlargement. No retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy is noted.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  The urinary bladder, distal ureters, uterus,
adnexa, sigmoid colon, and rectum are normal.  There is no free fluid in the
pelvis.  No pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy is noted.

BONE WINDOWS:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesion is identified.

IMPRESSION:  Limited evaluation on non-contrast-enhanced CT, without evidence
of peripancreatic fluid collection, stranding, or pseudocyst.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION: Poor venous access, request for PICC line for access.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ the procedure.  Dr. ___ was the
supervising physician.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the left brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a single lumen line measuring 26 cm in length was then placed
through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in a midline position,
with the tip in the left axillary/subclavian junction under fluoroscopic
guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film
of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided single lumen
catheter placement in a midline location, via the left brachial venous
approach.  Final internal length is 26 cm, with the tip positioned in the left
axillary/subclavian junction.  The line is ready to use.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with chronic pancreatitis with bacteremia with
IV needed for pain control, antibiotics and hydration.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the procedure.
Dr. ___ was the supervising physician.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering a total of 1 mg
of Versed and 50 mcg of Fentanyl for the 5 minute intraservice time during
which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored. 1%
lidocaine was used for local anesthesia.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  After review of the risks and benefits of the
procedure, informed consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The left side of
the neck and upper chest were prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Access was obtained into the left internal jugular vein under ultrasound
guidance.  A micropuncture needle was used for initial access.  A 0.018 wire
was passed through the needle.  The left internal jugular vein was noted to be
occluded just superior to the junction of the brachiocephalic veins and the
0.018 wire could not be advanced further.  The procedure was therefore
terminated.  Findings were discussed with ___.  No immediate
complications were noted.

IMPRESSION:  Triple-lumen catheter via left internal jugular was not
successful secondary to presence of clot within the left internal jugular vein
just superior to the junction of the right and left brachiocephalic veins. The
procedure was terminated.  Findings were discussed with ___.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ female with chronic pancreatitis and
surgical J-tube in place which patient reports has not been working properly. 
Evaluate J-tube function.

J-TUBE FLUOROSCOPY:  The J-tube was unwrapped by the patient and visually
inspected.  The external portion of the tube was visually degraded with a
region along the tubing which had been circumferentially repaired by the
patient in an ad-hoc manner ("hot glue").  

The tube was injected with water-soluble contrast.  Contrast flows freely
through the tube and enters into the small bowel.

IMPRESSION:  Degraded jejunostomy tube repaired in an ad-hoc manner by the
patient--recommend replacement.

The tube communicates freely with the jejunum.

These findings were communicated to Dr. ___ by telephone at 4:00
p.m. on ___.
